espn-604012.headline: Playing for fifth, with first in the world on offer
beats: Ireland finished their pool on 24 points, two more than South Africa, and beat them 20–17 on 21 November. South Africa play France in the final. Ireland play Australia for fifth.
Win by any margin and Ireland go top of the world rankings, above South Africa. Andy Farrell is treating the game as a dry run for next year's World Cup, which is a fair use of a fifth-place final.
Ireland won 33–31 when the sides met in Australia on 4 July. Since then Australia have conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand and 45 to England. They did win their last game, 29–26 in Wales.
Australia do not play again until a World Cup game against Hong Kong in October. Ireland's next Test is England in February, the side that kept them out of the third-place final by a point.

espn-604013.headline: Japan were seven short of Wales. Then came 145 points
beats: Three weeks ago in Cardiff, Wales beat Japan 28–21. Since then England have put 78 on Japan and Scotland 67, with Japan scoring 20 in reply across the two.

Wales went the other way. They beat New Zealand 35–28, their first win over them since 1953, then lost 26–29 to Australia after being wasteful in the red zone, as Gwyn Jones put it. Steve Tandy has made five changes for this one, with James Botham back in the back row and Jac Morgan on the bench.
At stake is ninth place in the Nations Championship. Japan need to win by 16 or more to go above Wales in the world rankings, which is a lot to ask of a side that has just shipped 145.
Wales go to France in Paris in February. Japan have nothing scheduled after this, so whatever they take home has to last.

espn-604014.headline: England have never beaten New Zealand three in a row
beats: Their 37–12 win at home on 21 November was England's biggest over New Zealand. It was also their second in a row, a pair they had not managed since 2002-03. The third-place final puts the same two sides back in London.

New Zealand won their first four pool games, then lost to Wales and England. Dave Rennie rated the England defeat worse than Wales, a game he said let the country down. He has made six changes, and Jordie Barrett captains for the first time with Codie Taylor injured.
England have won five straight, with at least five tries every time. Last week's margin was 25. Win by 16 or more and they go top of the world rankings, above South Africa, Ireland and France.
New Zealand's next Test is against Chile at the World Cup in October 2027. That is a long time to sit with a third straight defeat to England.

espn-604015.headline: Scotland win 67–5, then change eleven
beats: Only four starters survive the 67–5 win over Japan. Rory Darge, pulled from that side with a shoulder injury, is fit again and captains in place of the injured Sione Tuipulotu, and Finn Russell is back at fly-half.

Argentina lost 47–38 to Scotland in Cordoba in July and conceded 45 in Paris last weekend. Felipe Contepomi has put Zebre's Tobias Wade on the bench for a possible debut, ahead of Matias Moroni, who could have won his 100th cap.

This is the seventh-place final, but the ranking is looser than the table: win by 16 or more and Argentina go above Scotland into sixth. The last two meetings both finished nine points apart, one each way.
Scotland next see Italy in February. Argentina's next fixture is Canada at the World Cup in October 2027, which is a long time to sit on a result.

espn-604016.headline: Two points last time. This time, a trophy and No. 1
beats: France beat South Africa 21–19 on 13 November. They meet again in London in the grand final of the first Nations Championship, and a France win by any margin also takes them past South Africa and Ireland to first in the world rankings.

South Africa have lost their last two by five points combined, 19–21 to France and 17–20 to Ireland. They still finished top of the South and remain ranked first. France arrive on five straight wins, the last 45–17 over Argentina.

Thomas Ramos starts at full-back after a thigh problem kept him out since September, and takes the kicking back from Kalvin Gourgues. His last Test, in March, ended with his penalty in the closing seconds beating England 48–46 for a second straight Six Nations title.
The last meeting came down to two points. France have their closing-seconds kicker back.
